feature.summary: A workspace owner or admin can set a monthly credit limit with a mode of Off, Notify or Block. Only Block refuses members' Cloud turns once the month's spend reaches the limit. Decisions are cached for 60 seconds. A separate policy cap and a personal spend limit also exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Caps managed spend for a workspace per calendar month and optionally alerts at a percentage threshold.
purpose.why_it_exists: Finance owners need a budget ceiling (S82.31). Notify lets them watch before enforcing.
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins who hold the policy.manage permission; members feel the refusals.
problems_solved: No early warning before a budget is hit
use_cases: Owner sets a cap, 80 percent alert and Notify to observe first.
Owner switches to Block; members' new Cloud turns stop at the cap.
Owner raises the cap and members are freed at once.

where_to_find_it: Web and hosted desktop: workspace console usage page /workspace/usage, card 'Monthly spend limit' (apps/web/app/workspace/usage/page.tsx; apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceUsageAnalytics.tsx:377; WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:186-198).
Second control: Settings > workspace policy, 'Monthly spend cap' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/WorkspacePolicySection.tsx:630).
Personal limit (a different thing): Settings > Usage card 'Monthly spend limit' with 'Manage' (UsageSection.tsx:707-720).
prerequisites: Workspace membership and the policy.manage permission to change (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/spend-limit/route.ts:69).
The component renders nothing for a caller who cannot administer the limit (WorkspaceSpendLimit.test.tsx:133).
screens_and_controls: Usage bar and text '<spent> of <cap> used this month', '· over the limit' or '· past the N% alert' (WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:196-222).
Fields 'Cap (credits)', 'Alert at' %, select 'Spend limit enforcement' with Off, Notify, Block (lines 228-270).

Help text per mode: Off 'Recorded only. Nothing acts on the cap.'; Notify 'Crossing the cap is reported, but no turn is refused.'; Block 'Managed turns stop at the cap, up to about a minute of spend late.' (lines 76-80).
Buttons 'Set limit' or 'Update limit', and 'Remove limit' (lines 291-322).
journey: Enter a cap in credits, an alert percent and a mode.
If choosing Block when it was not Block, read the inline notice that new turns will be declined (line 278-289).
To remove, click 'Remove limit' and confirm the dialog 'Remove the workspace spend limit?'.
A member over the cap sees the refusal message.
feedback_and_outputs: Refusal text: 'This workspace has reached its monthly spend limit. An owner or admin can raise it, or wait until the limit resets at the start of next month.' (apps/web/lib/services/spend-limit-service.ts:187-190).
Policy-cap refusal uses the policy's reason with code organization_spend_cap_reached and status 402 (managed-usage-request-service.ts:399).
Save errors appear as an alert next to the buttons (WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:325-335).
settings: Monthly cap (credits), enforcement (off/notify/block), alert threshold percent (spend-limit route PutSchema, lines 40-46).

working: Limit CRUD: GET (state), PUT (upsert) and DELETE with CSRF, rate limits, permission check and audit event admin_policy_changed, critical severity when switching to block (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/spend-limit/route.ts:50-175).

Enforcement: evaluateSpendLimit allows unless configured, mode block and spend >= cap; decision cached 60 seconds; unreadable state is treated as allowed (apps/web/lib/services/spend-limit-service.ts:53-60, 161-206). A raised cap or delete clears the cache for this server process (lines 212-214, 245-275).

Gate applied before managed work in chat completions, embeddings, audio transcription, voice live sessions, image and video generation and resume routes (callers of buildSpendLimitGateResponse in apps/web/app/api/...); the gate answers 402 with type insufficient_quota (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:511-545).
Separate policy cap in the managed request path: refusal writes audit event spend_cap_exceeded and throws organization_spend_cap_reached (managed-usage-request-service.ts:338-399, 779).
Web UI with confirm dialog for removal.
incomplete: The confirmation dialog covers only removing the limit. Saving a change to Block shows an inline warning note, not a dialog (WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:278-322). The brief says the change is confirmed by the dialog.

Only the policy-cap path writes an audit event per refused request. The Block path writes a warning log line only (managed-compute-gate.ts:527-530). The brief's line 'each refused request writes an audit event' is true only for the policy cap.
The 60-second cache is per server process (Map in memory, spend-limit-service.ts:67); across several instances enforcement lag can differ. This is read from the code, not tested [inferred].
not_available: Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no controls (brief n/a). They show the refusal text only. Mobile treats organization_spend_cap_reached as no model switch (apps/mobile/services/apiErrors.ts:109); how other apps treat code over_cap was not established.

established.statement: An owner can set a spending cap that stops managed usage once reached.
Modes are off, notify and block; only block refuses.
Decisions are cached 60 seconds, so enforcement is eventual and may overshoot by about one window of spend.
If spend cannot be read, the request is allowed.
Product requirement: Usage settings must include a monthly spend limit.
An action a user cannot undo asks first, naming the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: With mode Block and spend at or above the cap, a member's next Cloud turn is refused with status 402 and the monthly spend limit message.
With mode Notify or Off, turns continue even above the cap.
Raising the cap frees members immediately on that server.
A member cannot see the set or remove controls.
Removing the limit shows a confirmation naming the consequence and then removes it.
Changing to Block records a critical audit event.
If the spend lookup fails, the turn is allowed and an error is logged.
inferred: Overshoot of about a minute of spend is acceptable and is stated to the admin in the UI copy [inferred from WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:79].
proposed: [proposed] Put switching to Block behind the confirmation dialog, since it starts refusing work.
[proposed] Merge the two cap mechanisms (limit table and policy cap) or document which wins.
[proposed] Write an audit event on each Block refusal.

steps.what_happens: Admin saves the limit; browser PUTs with bearer token and CSRF header.
Server checks membership and policy.manage, upserts the row, clears the cache, writes an audit event, returns the new state.
A member sends a managed request; the route calls the gate which resolves the funding organization and evaluates the limit (cache 60 s).
The month-to-date sum of completed requests for the whole organization is read with the privileged database adapter.
If blocked, the route answers 402 with the message; the client shows the refusal.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Not model specific. The sum uses actual cost of completed managed requests, whatever model or provider served them. Only managed (Cloud) turns are gated; own-key and Local turns are not.

gaps.gap: Two caps exist (organization_spend_limits via gate, policy monthlySpendCapCents via reservation) with different codes and UI.

corrections.claim: Limit CRUD: GET, PUT, DELETE with CSRF, rate limits, permission check and audit event admin_policy_changed, critical severity when switching to block (route.ts:50-175)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: PUT and DELETE check CSRF and rate limit. GET (route.ts:57-77) has no CSRF check, which is normal for a read. Audit is critical only on PUT when the saved mode is block (route.ts:116-130). Any PUT that saves mode block records critical, not only a switch to block. DELETE records a warning audit event, and only if a row was removed (route.ts:144-156). GET writes no audit event.
corrections.correction: PUT and DELETE check CSRF, rate limit and policy.manage. PUT audits admin_policy_changed with severity critical whenever the saved mode is block, otherwise warning. DELETE audits a warning only when a row existed. GET is rate limited and membership checked only.

corrections.claim: Permissions: policy.manage to change; GET passes requireOrgMember and requireTeamAdminAccess. Whether non-admins can read is unclear. Subscription: plan names for access are not read in this review. Unknown: which plan tiers can reach it.
corrections.what_the_code_shows: requireTeamAdminAccess asserts active membership. It then throws SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED 403 unless the organization's plan allows the team_admin capability, with the message 'Team administration requires an active Team or Enterprise subscription' and requiredPlans team and enterprise. GET and PUT/DELETE both run it. GET does not need policy.manage, so any active member of a team or enterprise workspace can read the state; canManageLimit tells the UI whether to show controls. The limit is not readable or settable on other plans.
corrections.correction: Subscription: Team or Enterprise only (403 SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED otherwise). Read: any active member of such a workspace. Write: also needs policy.manage. This also means the 'Unknown' entries about plan tiers and member read can be resolved from code.

corrections.claim: Cap decisions only for Cloud turns; Local and own-key turns are not gated; how other apps treat over_cap was not established
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The gate sits on the managed llm/v1 routes only, so Local and own-key traffic that does not use them is not gated. That part holds. The web chat does handle these codes: voice-input-store.ts, live-voice-session.ts and the useDictation test reference over_cap or organization_spend_cap_reached. Mobile apiErrors.ts lists organization_spend_cap_reached as no-model-switch, but not over_cap.
corrections.correction: Web voice code handles both codes. Mobile's no-model-switch list has organization_spend_cap_reached but not over_cap, so over_cap would offer a model switch on mobile.

missing_facts: Access needs a Team or Enterprise plan. requireTeamAdminAccess throws 403 SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED for any other plan, on GET as well as PUT and DELETE (apps/web/app/api/settings/team/team-admin-access.ts:70-90; spend-limit/route.ts:63, 79). The page lists this as unknown.

The budget is resolved from the user's first governing organization and ignores the x-agi-organization-id header, so a member cannot escape the cap by sending 'personal' (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:507-525; apps/web/lib/services/enterprise-funding-organization.ts:15-23). The page does not say this.

Web chat has client handling for the over_cap and organization_spend_cap_reached codes in voice code (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts, apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts), which the page lists as unknown. Mobile's no-model-switch list omits over_cap (apps/mobile/services/apiErrors.ts:99-109).
